elements.quote: Fourteen of the studies were cross sectional, four were cohort and one case control studies. A total of 8755 participants with the smallest 166 to the largest 1069 participants included and found the prevalence which ranges from 6.80 to 25.4% of SSI following cesarean section in Ethiopia. On the other hand, the quality of each study was assessed by using NOS, the score of all included studies lies between 8 to 9 which indicates good quality (Table 1) (1).
elements.reason: The manuscript summarizes the characteristics of the included studies (study design, participant numbers, prevalence range) and the risk of bias (using NOS scores) for the synthesis.

elements.quote: Eventually, 19 articles were found eligible for inclusion in the final SRMA (Fig 1). Among the studies included in this SRMA, six studies were in Amhara, four in SNNP region, two in Oromia, two in Addis Ababa, two in Harari, one in Dire Dawa and two in Tigray.
elements.reason: The studies contributing to the synthesis are identified by their regional distribution and total count (19 articles).

elements.quote: The pooled estimate of SSI in Ethiopia was 11.13% (95%CI, 9.2912.97%). Prolonged labor (AOR = 3.16, 95% CI; (2.14-4.68)), chorioamnionitis (AOR = 4.26, 95% CI; (1.99-8.91)), prolonged PROM (AOR = 3.80, 95% CI; (2.51-5.62)), repeated vaginal examination (AOR = 3.80, 95% CI; (2.45-5.88)), decreased hemoglobin level (AOR = 4.57, 95%CI; (3.16-6.60)), vertical skin incision (AOR = 3.09, 95% CI; (2.04-4.67)) and general anesthesia (AOR = 1.82, 95% CI (1.21-2.75)) are significantly associated with SSI after cesarean section in Ethiopia.
elements.reason: The manuscript reports the results of the meta-analysis for the pooled prevalence of SSI and the pooled adjusted odds ratios for various predictors.

elements.quote: The finding of this SRMA showed that the pooled prevalence of surgical site infection after cesarean section in Ethiopia was 11.13% (95% CI: 9.29, 12.97%)
